text.en: What would you do if hail destroyed your whole crop? Lencho, a farmer, wrote to God. Today we read what happened.

Lencho is a farmer whose field of ripe corn needs only a good rain to be ready. His house stands alone on a hill in a valley.
The rain came, but it turned into hail. The hailstones destroyed the whole crop, and Lencho's family faced a year of hunger.
Lencho had a simple, deep faith in God, so he wrote a letter to God asking for a hundred pesos to sow his field again.
The postmaster laughed when he read the address, then became serious and admired Lencho's faith. He decided to answer the letter.
The postmaster and his employees collected money, but could send only a little more than half of the amount. They signed the envelope God.
Lencho was not surprised to receive the money, but he became angry when he counted it.
He wrote again, saying only seventy pesos had reached him, and asked God to send the rest, but not through the mail because post office employees were a bunch of crooks.
The story is ironic: Lencho trusted God but accused the people who helped him. It shows faith, human kindness and misunderstanding.

problem.en: Lencho asked for 100 pesos and received 70. How many pesos were short?

text.en: Subtract the amount received from the amount asked.

why.en: This is why Lencho wrote again.

prompt.en: Explain what the story tells us about faith and kindness.

requiredIdeas.en: The irony of Lencho calling the helpers crooks

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the postmaster kept the money

points.en: Lencho's crop was ruined by hail and he wrote to God.
The postmaster and staff sent about seventy pesos.
Lencho wrongly blamed the post office.
The story shows faith and irony.
